extracted.intended_audience: general TED viewers; people interested in spoken-word poetry and social-justice storytelling
extracted.subtask_description: A short, performed spoken‑word/poetry piece presented as a TED Talk that emphasizes emotional honesty and social themes (courage, silence, injustice). Intended as a brief, powerful personal/performative essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity (short)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece should be concise — suited to the TED Talk/short video format — delivering impact within a limited runtime. Aim for a compact structure that communicates its point without unnecessary length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional power / authenticity ("from the heart")
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as a "powerful piece from the heart."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The work should convey genuine feeling and personal conviction. Authentic voice and emotionally resonant language/ delivery are emphasized over abstract or detached argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to the unsaid / use silence as rhetorical material
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted line: "We spend so much time listening to the things people are saying that we rarely pay attention to the things they don't."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate attention to what is omitted or unspoken as a theme or device — exploring absence, silence, or omission to reveal meaning and provoke reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme: courage to speak up against ignorance and injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: Page states the talk is "about finding the courage to speak up against ignorance and injustice."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central thematic thrust should focus on moral courage and speaking out; content should engage with issues of ignorance and injustice and motivate or illustrate the act of speaking up rather than remaining silent.
